Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Ashish Joshi, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
Mrs. Neetu Singh, learned counsel for the 
caveator.
Though these are three writ-petitions but in
WPMS No.1481 of 2023 learned counsel for the 
parties agree, that the issue involved in this writ￾petition happens to be distinct from the other two 
writ-petitions.
Hence, WPMS No.1481 of 2023 is directed to 
be delinked from the Bunch and will be listed 
separately.
Misc. Application No.IA/3/2023 filed by the 
respondent in WPMS No.1481 of 2023 is allowed 
and the counter affidavit is taken on record.
Urgency Application No.IA/4/2023 too 
would stand allowed.
The same is directed to be listed in the week 
commencing 30.10.2023.
Learned counsel for the petitioner presses 
the Stay Application No.IA/1/2023 and  IA/2/2023, on the ground, that the workman has 
placed the award dated 27.01.2023 in Execution. 
As far as the execution of the award is concerned, 
that will be kept in abeyance, subject to the 
limited extend, that so far as it relates to the 
reinstatement, but as far as other arrears, which 
have been directed to be paid, there operates no 
interim order, the same would be deposited.
In WPMS No.2964 of 2022, Misc. 
Application No.IA/2/2023 would stand allowed. 
The counter affidavit filed by the 
workman/respondent through Misc. Application 
No.IA/2/2023 is taken on record.
The interim order dated 21.12.2022 would 
remain extended till the next date of listing.
In WPMS No.1475 of 2023, the respondent 
has not yet filed counter affidavit nor does 
anyone represent him.
As such, since the issue involved was the 
same as in WPMS No.2964 of 2022, the bearing 
of interim order dated 21.12.2022 would also be 
applicable in the connected writ-petition.
Let a copy of this order be also placed in the 
connected writ-petitions 
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 25.09.2023 Sukhbant
